finding.claim: Visibility inverse mapping fails open: any mode other than 0644/0600 is reported as PUBLIC, so cross-filesystem copy with default retain_visibility can write a world-readable (0644) destination from a non-standard private source mode (e.g. 0640, 0700).
finding.source: Source file mode on the source mount (set by operator, not attacker-controlled); attacker must be able to trigger a cross-mount copy or move.
finding.sink: MountManager::copyAcrossFilesystem writes destination visibility from inverted source mode (src/MountManager.php:398-404) -> adapter forFile(PUBLIC) -> 0644.

trace.note: copy() routes to copyAcrossFilesystem when source and destination filesystems differ
retain_visibility default true; reads source visibility when no explicit visibility is configured
calls $sourceFilesystem->visibility($sourcePath); adapter (not in repo) maps mode via inverseForFile
inverseForFile begins mapping by exact equality to filePublic/filePrivate only
unrecognized mode falls through to 'return Visibility::PUBLIC; // default'
PUBLIC is merged into config and passed to destination writeStream

finding.guards_checked: PortableVisibilityGuard::guardAgainstInvalidInput (src/PortableVisibilityGuard.php:9-17) validates only caller-supplied strings, not inbound modes; Filesystem::resolveConfigForMoveAndCopy (src/Filesystem.php:282-297) is not on this path because MountManager builds its own config; no fail-closed branch in inverse mapping. Same pattern in inverseForDirectory (lines 50-59). Adapter code is not in this repo, so whether the official local adapter calls inverseForFile on this path is unverified (PLAUSIBLE).

finding.claim: Public URLs are built by plain concatenation of the normalized path with no percent-encoding; the normalizer permits '?', '#' and literal '%2e%2e' segments, so user-chosen object names can produce links that resolve to a different object or escape the configured prefix.
finding.source: User-chosen object name (e.g. upload filename) passed to Filesystem::publicUrl.
finding.sink: PrefixPublicUrlGenerator::publicUrl and ShardedPrefixPublicUrlGenerator::publicUrl return an unescaped URL built from the path.

trace.note: only Unicode category C characters are rejected; '?', '#', '%' pass through
segments are not percent-decoded, so '%2e%2e' is kept as an ordinary segment
returns prefixer->prefixPath($path), a raw concatenation with no rawurlencode
same raw concatenation on the sharded path

finding.guards_checked: Only the Unicode category C check in WhitespacePathNormalizer. No URL encoding in PathPrefixer::prefixPath or either generator. Browser dot-segment normalization of %2e%2e is standard WHATWG URL behavior but was not tested against a live CDN (PLAUSIBLE, low). Impact depends on the consuming app exposing generated links for user-chosen names.
